text:
Predicates:
ZahaHadid(x) ::: x is a Zaha Hadid design style.
MaxAdores(x) ::: Max adores x.
InterestingGeometries(x) ::: x has interesting geometries.
Brutalist(x) ::: x is a brutalist building.
KellyWearstler(x) ::: x is a Kelly Wearstler design style.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
Design(x) ::: x is a design.
Premises:
∀x ((ZahaHadid(x) ∧ MaxAdores(x)) → InterestingGeometries(x)) ::: All of Zaha Hadid's design styles that Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x ((Brutalist(x) ∧ MaxAdores(x)) → ¬InterestingGeometries(x)) ::: No brutalist buildings that Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x (MaxAdores(x) → (ZahaHadid(x) ∨ KellyWearstler(x))) ::: Every style that Max adores is either Zaha Hadid's design style or Kelly Wearstler's design style.
∀x ((KellyWearstler(x) ∧ MaxAdores(x)) → Evocative(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles that Max adores are evocative.
∀x ((KellyWearstler(x) ∧ MaxAdores(x)) → Dreamy(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles that Max adores are dreamy.
∀x ((Design(x) ∧ MaxAdores(x) ∧ InterestingGeometries(x)) → (Brutalist(x) ∧ Evocative(x))) ::: If a design by Max that he adores has interesting geometries, then the design is a brutalist building and evocative.
Conclusion:
∃x (Design(x) ∧ Brutalist(x)) ::: A design by Max is a brutalist building.
